unit.brief: THE WHOLE BRIEF IS A FILE: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-supdb/2fecfb3d-3630-50b2-b9c5-2a19705f39b6/scratchpad/plan/build/T22/brief.txt. Read all of it before anything else and again before you answer; it is this change's section, and what follows here is only its outline. Stage G1 is closed and one change after it has landed (git log says where the branch stands; scratch/plan/build/close/g1-built.md is the closing critic's account). This is the second change after it, from the critic's concern 3: the CI group cross-arm (the library's unit tests built for aarch64 and run under qemu-user 8.2.2) died in two parallel runs of five with "QEMU internal SIGSEGV {code=MAPERR, addr=0x20}" and no test failed; green one test at a time; nobody has diagnosed it. The change: reproduce and measure with the test binary run directly under the emulator (no cargo in the loop); find what is in flight when it dies (qemu's own -strace, filters by module and test, the tests added since 19d078d1 as first suspects); say whose bug it is with evidence before anything changes (QEMU's own defect on a legitimate sequence of guest syscalls, or the program touching a range it does not own, which would be a real defect on every platform and is then the fix); then the smallest thing that makes the group give a verdict: the fewest tests compiled out of the emulated run alone, each shown to matter and each still run natively, or failing that the fragile modules one test at a time in the group's case of scripts/check.sh. Shown by the rate before and after (at least twenty clean runs after, with the arithmetic), by exactly which tests the emulated run lost, and by the group green three times by exit status. No test skipped or loosened on the native target, no retry, no blanket single thread unless the evidence leaves nothing else, no engine change unless the engine is at fault, no timing, and nothing done with upstream's branch (the owner, 22 Nov). How an agent waits, the commit this begins at, running one heavy thing at a time, and the disk are in the file.
